notes: C04 RESOLVED: Extracted primary source package https://arxiv.org/e-print/2103.17009 (Cardiel et al. 2021, MNRAS 504, 3730, paper_RGB.tex Table median_RGB_table, lines 1238-1279) and verified companion portal https://guaix.ucm.es/rgbphot (HTTP 200). The 35 rows of Table median_RGB_table (3990 to 7210 AA, 100 AA steps with 3990/7210 zero endpoints) match SVO Generic/UCM.b, .g, .r exactly. response_unit: dimensionless peak-normalized median sensitivity (0-1); defined for photon-counting synthetic photometry in Cardiel et al. (2021) Eqs. 4-5 (note: SVO metadata labels DetectorType=0)

source_name: Jiang, Liu, Gu & Susstrunk (2013) Camera Spectral Sensitivity Database (RIT / Columbia / EPFL)
evidence: Inspected camspec_database.txt (24,473 bytes) and camlist&equipment.txt (848 bytes, HTTP 200): tabulates R, G, B relative spectral sensitivity across 33 wavelengths (400-720 nm in 10 nm steps) measured with a monochromator, integrating sphere, and PR655 spectroradiometer.
notes: Combined internal IR-cut filter + Bayer CFA microlens + CMOS/CCD sensor spectral sensitivity. Licensed under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 on landing page (non-commercial restriction applies to mirroring).
wavelength_unit: nm (400 to 720 nm in 10 nm steps, 33 points)
response_unit: dimensionless normalized camera spectral sensitivity (R, G, B columns)
retrieval_instructions: GET http://www.gujinwei.org/research/camspec/camspec_database.txt (24,473 bytes) and http://www.gujinwei.org/research/camspec/camlist&equipment.txt (848 bytes). In camspec_database.txt, each camera block consists of 1 line with the camera model name followed by 33 lines of 3 whitespace-separated floats (Red, Green, Blue sensitivity on the uniform 400:10:720 nm grid). Validated all 28 camera blocks in camspec_database.txt. Note: for Cameras/Canon, SVO also includes 1DMarkII_B/G/R and 450D-IR_B/G/R (from Mauer 2009), and for Cameras/Hasselblad SVO also includes H3D_B/G/R (from Mauer 2009), which are fetched via SVO fallback.
search_notes: Inspected entire camspec_database.txt (all 28 cameras) and SVO browse lists for Cameras/Canon. Combined lens/internal-filter/Bayer-CFA/sensor spectral sensitivity measured with PR655 spectroradiometer and monochromator (Jiang et al. 2013); separate Bayer CFA and bare CMOS/CCD QE curves are not in the database. Redistribution note: landing page http://www.gujinwei.org/research/camspec/db.html states CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0; preserved as author page statement, not an independent legal clearance.

notes: MERIS is a programmable 15-band grating imaging spectrometer (scrambler + refractive optics + concave diffraction grating + thinned back-illuminated CCD arrays); published curves are combined spectral channel response profiles (bandpass functions), not separable physical filters.
wavelength_unit: nm (both in ESA MERIS_NominalSRF_Model2004.xlsx and NASA OBPG meris_rsrs_avg.txt)
response_unit: dimensionless peak-normalized spectral response function (0-1); photon/energy convention not stated in header (SVO labels DetectorType=0)
retrieval_instructions: Download https://oceandata.sci.gsfc.nasa.gov/rsr_tables/images/rsr/meris_rsrs_avg.txt (parse after '/end_header', Col 1 = wavelength [nm], Cols 2..16 = b1..b15, filtering out -999.0 fill values) or download ESA MERIS_NominalSRF_Model2004.xlsx and read sheet2 paired (wavelength, SRF) columns for bands 1..15.
search_notes: Verified both ESA Earth Online Model 2004 Excel workbook and NASA OBPG ASCII table.

source_name: AAVSO Photometric All-Sky Survey (APASS) Reference Passbands via SVO
evidence: Inspected all 6 SVO VOTable headers for Misc/APASS (B, V, sdss_g, sdss_r, sdss_i, sdss_z; all DetectorType=0): PARAM Description explicitly states 'APASS B filter, defined as identical to GCPD/Johnson.B_Landolt', 'APASS V filter, defined as identical to GCPD/Johnson.V_Landolt', and 'APASS g/r/i/z filter, defined as identical to SLOAN/SDSS.g/r/i/z'.
conditions: Composite alias system: Landolt B,V + SDSS g,r,i,z (airmass 1.3 in SDSS)
notes: Critical scientific pitfall: SVO Misc/APASS does NOT tabulate independent physical measurements of the APASS ASA 0.2m astrograph / Apogee U16m (KAF-16803 CCD) / Astrodon Johnson B,V and Sloan g',r',i',z' hardware. Instead, SVO defines Misc/APASS.B and .V as exact aliases of GCPD/Johnson.B_Landolt and .V_Landolt, and Misc/APASS.sdss_g/r/i/z as exact aliases of SLOAN/SDSS.g/r/i/z (with DetectorType=0). Checked VizieR II/336 (Henden et al. 2015 APASS DR9), which is a photometric catalog without separate hardware transmission tables.
response_unit: dimensionless normalized response (identical to GCPD/Johnson.B_Landolt, V_Landolt and SLOAN/SDSS.g,r,i,z)
retrieval_instructions: Fetch SVO VOTables https://svo2.cab.inta-csic.es/theory/fps/fps.php?ID=Misc/APASS.<Band> for B, V, sdss_g, sdss_r, sdss_i, sdss_z, or link directly to GCPD/Johnson.B_Landolt, V_Landolt and SLOAN/SDSS.g,r,i,z.
search_notes: Inspected all 6 SVO VOTables and VizieR II/336; confirmed Misc/APASS in SVO is a pure alias to Landolt B,V and SDSS g,r,i,z.

source_name: Tonry et al. (2018, PASP 130, 064505) ATLAS c and o System Bandpasses (arXiv:1802.00879 atlas_defn.tex Table 2)
evidence: Downloaded and inspected arXiv:1802.00879 source tarball (Tonry et al. 2018, atlas_defn.tex lines 2256-2292, Table 2 \label{tab:coband} 'ATLAS c and o Bandpasses'): tabulates Wavelength [nm] (5 nm steps: 400-680 nm for T_c, 550-830 nm for T_o) and total system transmission T_c, T_o. Table comments explicitly state: 'The transmission includes 1.2 airmasses of atmosphere, mirror reflection and AR coatings, filter transmission calculated for an f/2 beam, and detector QE.' Also inspected FIG/qe_acams.pdf and FIG/filters.pdf inside the tarball: decompressed PDF streams confirm they are embedded raster images (/Im0 Do, 1,920,000 bytes), not vector numeric tables. Compared with SVO Misc/Atlas.cyan (248 rows, 4110-6580 AA, 10 AA step) and .orange (273 rows, 5550-8270 AA, 10 AA step).
conditions: Includes 1.2 airmasses of atmosphere, 0.92 overcoated Al mirror reflectivity, Schmidt corrector/field lens AR coatings, Materion (Barr) f/2 filter (n=2), and STA-1600 CCD QE at -50 C
notes: Tonry et al. (2018) Eq. 2 & Table 3 define bandpass pivot wavelength and photon etendue using photon-counting AB synthetic photometry (int lambda T(nu) d ln nu), whereas SVO labels Misc/Atlas DetectorType=0. Also note a slight sampling/interpolation difference at band edges between Tonry et al. Table 2 (5 nm grid; e.g. T_c(420 nm)=0.137, T_o(560 nm)=0.111) and SVO Misc/Atlas (10 AA = 1 nm grid). Component curves (STA-1600 QE in Fig. 6 left, filter+optics+atm in Fig. 6 right) are embedded raster bitmaps in FIG/qe_acams.pdf and FIG/filters.pdf, not published as separate ASCII tables.
wavelength_unit: nm (in Tonry et al. 2018 Table 2, 5 nm step); Angstrom (in SVO Misc/Atlas, 10 AA step)
response_unit: dimensionless total system throughput fraction (0-1, including 1.2 airmass atmosphere, optics, filter, and STA-1600 CCD QE)
retrieval_instructions: Download https://arxiv.org/e-print/1802.00879 (tar.gz) and extract atlas_defn.tex, Table 2 (\label{tab:coband}, lines 2256-2292): cols 1-6 give (lambda [nm], T_c) wrapped across 3 column pairs from 400 to 680 nm (57 points); cols 7-12 give (lambda [nm], T_o) wrapped across 3 column pairs from 550 to 830 nm (57 points). Or fetch 1 nm interpolated curves from SVO https://svo2.cab.inta-csic.es/theory/fps/fps.php?ID=Misc/Atlas.cyan and .orange.
search_notes: Inspected full LaTeX source and decompressed PDF streams of FIG/qe_acams.pdf and FIG/filters.pdf in arXiv:1802.00879; confirmed separate component curves are raster-only.
